A screening programme finds 12 true positives and 36 false positives. What percentage of positive results are correct? 12/(12 + 36) = 12/48 = 25%.

An anchor is a number you meet first, and it pulls later estimates towards it even when it is plainly irrelevant. Tversky and Kahneman spun a wheel rigged to stop at 10 or 65. They then asked what percentage of United Nations members were African countries. Those who saw the higher number guessed higher. Anchoring bias is the pull of a starting number on an estimate, even a number known to be random.
After the wheel stopped on 10, the median estimate was 25%. After it stopped on 65, the median estimate was 45%. The number was plainly irrelevant, yet it moved the typical estimate by that gap.

The anchoring index divides the gap between median estimates by the gap between anchors. An index of 0 means the anchor was ignored. An index of 1 means estimates moved as far as the anchors did. Anchors of 0 and 100 with medians of 30 and 50 give 20 ÷ 100 = 0.2. The index measures how much of the anchors' gap shows up in the estimates.

Find the anchoring index for anchors of 10 and 70 with median estimates of 30 and 51. Find the gap between the medians. 51 − 30 = 21 Find the gap between the anchors. 70 − 10 = 60 Divide the first gap by the second. 21 ÷ 60 = 0.35

Anchors of 20 and 80 were used, and the median estimates of an oak tree's age were 35 and 59 years. Estimates moved 0.4 of the way between the anchors. Even random starting numbers pull estimates a long way.

Are there more English words that start with k, or more that have k as the third letter? Most people say start. Now count. Words with k third are about twice as common, yet words that start with k are easier to call to mind. Judging how common something is by how easily examples come to mind is the availability heuristic.

A bat and a ball cost £1.10 together. The bat costs £1.00 more than the ball. The answer that springs to mind, 10p, would make the total £1.20. Kahneman calls the quick answer System 1 and the check System 2. These are names for fast and deliberate thinking, not two brain organs. Intuition is often right; the skill is knowing when to check.
Anchors of 100 and 500 produce median estimates of 220 and 340. What is the anchoring index? (340 − 220)/(500 − 100) = 120/400 = 0.3.

After several news reports of shark attacks, a swimmer judges sharks a bigger risk than drowning. Judging frequency by how easily examples come to mind is which heuristic? The availability heuristic: vivid, easily recalled cases feel common.
A pen and a notebook cost £2.20 together. The notebook costs £2.00 more than the pen. How much does the pen cost, in pence? Pen x, notebook x + 200: 2x + 200 = 220, so x = 10p.
Which jacket is more likely to feel like a bargain? The one with the “was £200” tag: the higher number makes £120 feel low.
What made the wheel experiment striking? The wheel was plainly random, yet it still pulled the estimates.
By how many percentage points did the medians differ? 45 − 25 = 20 percentage points.
Anchors of 0 and 40 produce median estimates of 10 and 30. What is the anchoring index? (30 − 10) ÷ (40 − 0) = 20 ÷ 40 = 0.5.
What does an index of 0.35 say about the anchors? An index between 0 and 1 shows how far the estimates moved, as a share of the anchors' gap.
What is the anchoring index, (difference in medians) ÷ (difference in anchors)? (59 − 35)/(80 − 20) = 24/60 = 0.4.

In a sample of 600 English words containing k, 200 start with k and 400 have k as the third letter. What percentage start with k? Give one decimal place. 200/600 = 0.333, or 33.3%: words with k third are twice as common, though harder to recall.
How much does the ball cost, in pence? Ball x, bat x + 100p: 2x + 100 = 110, so x = 5p. The intuitive 10p would make the total £1.20.
Mould on a loaf doubles its area every day and covers the whole loaf on day 12. On which day did it cover half the loaf? Doubling means it was half the size one day earlier: day 11.
Anchors of 10 and 60 produce median estimates of 30 and 40. What is the anchoring index? (40 − 30)/(60 − 10) = 10/50 = 0.2.

Conformity is giving the group's answer even when your own eyes say otherwise. Asch had people match line lengths after several confederates gave the same wrong answer. Alone, people erred on under 1% of judgements. A critical answer is one given after the majority has spoken wrongly. To measure conformity, count the critical answers that follow the wrong majority.

In a line-judgement replication, 18 people each gave 12 critical answers. Of all those answers, 72 followed the wrong majority. About a third of critical answers went along, as Asch found. Most answers stayed independent, and about a quarter of people never yielded.

Obedience is following an authority's instruction, and it weakens as the victim gets closer. In Milgram's 1963 study, participants told to shock a learner for errors were urged on by an experimenter. The learner was an actor and no shocks were real. In the same room, 16 of 40 went on to the end. Obedience is measured by the share who go on to the final 450-volt switch.

In Milgram's baseline condition, 26 of 40 participants continued to the final 450-volt switch. Most continued, though the learner was an actor and no shocks were real. Few people predicted that before the study.

In the touch-proximity condition, the participant had to press the learner's hand onto a shock plate. 12 of 40 continued to the end. Closeness weakened obedience but did not remove it. Burger's 2009 partial replication stopped at 150 volts: 70% were willing to continue, against 82.5% in Milgram's comparable condition. Gina Perry's archives found that experimenters sometimes left the script and many participants doubted the shocks. Obedience is real; the exact percentages depend on setting and belief.

More witnesses spread responsibility, so each person is less likely to act. Darley and Latané staged a seizure over an intercom. 85% of those who thought they alone heard it helped, against 31% who thought four others heard. If n people each act independently with chance p, at least one acts with chance 1 − (1 − p)ⁿ. More people give more chances, but each person's own chance can fall.

Five bystanders each independently act with probability 0.2. Even a low chance each gives a fair chance that someone acts. The famous 38 silent witnesses to the Genovese murder is largely a myth. CCTV of 219 real street conflicts showed that someone intervened in 91%.
Three bystanders each independently help with probability 0.5. What is the probability, as a percentage, that at least one helps? P(nobody) = 0.5³ = 0.125; P(at least one) = 0.875, or 87.5%.
Which statement fits the evidence from CCTV recordings of real public conflicts? Philpot and colleagues (2020) found intervention in 91% of 219 conflicts, rising with the number of bystanders.

Milgram's baseline had 26 of 40 obeying to the end; the same-room condition had 16 of 40. By how many percentage points did obedience fall? 26/40 = 65% and 16/40 = 40%; 65 − 40 = 25 percentage points.

On the crowded platform, how does the chance that one given person helps compare with the empty platform? Lower: with many onlookers each person feels less responsible and may assume someone else will act.
In a study, 15 of 50 critical answers followed the wrong majority. What percentage is that? 15 ÷ 50 = 0.3, or 30%.
What percentage of critical answers conformed? Give one decimal place. 18 × 12 = 216 critical answers; 72/216 = 0.333, or 33.3%.
In the same-room condition, 16 of 40 participants went on to the end. What percentage is that? 16 ÷ 40 = 0.4, or 40%.
What percentage is that? 26/40 = 0.65, or 65%.

In the baseline condition 26 of 40 obeyed to the end, and in the touch-proximity condition 12 of 40 did. By how many percentage points did obedience fall? 26/40 = 65% and 12/40 = 30%; 65 − 30 = 35 percentage points.

What is the probability, as a percentage, that at least one acts? Give one decimal place. P(nobody acts) = 0.8⁵ = 0.32768; P(at least one) = 1 − 0.32768 = 0.67232, or 67.2%.
In a conformity study, 21 of 60 critical answers follow the wrong majority. What percentage conformed? 21/60 = 0.35, or 35%.
Two bystanders each independently act with probability 0.4. What is the probability, as a percentage, that at least one acts? 1 − 0.6² = 1 − 0.36 = 0.64, or 64%.
